rationale: The workflow repeatedly fetches Python dependencies (pip installs for nose, unittest2, get-pip.py, version-specific wheels) across every matrix cell with no dependency cache. Evidence from a measured CI workflow on a fork (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) shows adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip with a key derived from the dependency manifest and restore-keys for fallback. The literature pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (Cache dependency downloads) also supports caching dependency downloads, with preconditions of repeated dependency fetching and cache inputs including lockfile/environment, both of which are present. The change is minimal: one cache step added after checkout in the tests job, before the pip setup steps. It preserves all build and test coverage, adds no new network access beyond the existing pip downloads, uses only read contents permissions, and the restore-keys provide safe fallback on cache miss. The workflow already has fail-fast: true, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is already satisfied.
